# Mod format

<!-- Generated by pfmod from the game's mod loader. Don't edit by hand. -->

A mod is a folder, or a `.zip` of one, in the game's mods folder. Its name is the mod's id. A zip may hold the files at its root or inside one folder.

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `mod.json` | Required. Who made it, see below |
| `icon.png` | Optional. Square, at most 128x128 |
| `theme.json` + `theme/...` | Optional. Restyles the interface, see Themes |
| `main.lua` + other `.lua` | Optional. An addon, see the API reference |
| `assets/sprites/ui/...`, `assets/fonts/...` | Replaces the interface's own art and fonts, see Game files |
| `monsters/...`, `items/...`, `login/background...` | Replaces monster art and cries and item icons, by id, and the login background |
| `README.txt`, `LICENSE`, ... | `.txt`, `.md` and files without an extension at the root are ignored |

## mod.json

```json
{
  "name": "My Mod",
  "version": "1.0",
  "author": "You",
  "description": "What this mod changes.",
  "weblink": "https://pokefields.com/forums/mods"
}
```

`name` (at most 48 characters), `version` (16) and `author` (32) are required; `description` (300) and `weblink` (200) are optional. Nothing else may be in it.

## Monsters and items

`<species>` is 1-649, written without leading zeros. `<form>` is 1-255 and only for a species' alternate shapes.

| Path | Image |
|---|---|
| `monsters/front/<species>[-<form>][-shiny].png` | Battle sprite seen from the front: square cells of 16-256 px |
| `monsters/back/<species>[-<form>][-shiny].png` | The same from behind |
| `monsters/icon/<species>.png` | Box icon, 32x32 |
| `monsters/follower/<species>[-shiny].png` | Walking sprite: 2 columns (steps) x 4 rows (up, down, left, right) of square cells, 16-128 px |
| `monsters/cry/<species>.ogg` or `.wav` | Cry |
| `items/<item>.png` | Item icon, 32x32. Clothing cannot be replaced |
| `login/background.png` or `.ogv` | The login screen's background: an image (at most 4096x4096), or a looping Ogg Theora video. It covers the screen, cropping what does not fit |

A follower for a species that has no walking sprite in the game (494-649) makes it walk, for you and for everyone who has the same mod.

### Battle sprites

A battle sprite is one row of square cells, played left to right, 100 ms each. The bottom centre of a cell is where the monster stands. A `.json` beside it, with the same name, changes how it plays:

```json
{"frame_ms": [100, 80, 120], "order": [0, 1, 0], "columns": 2}
```

- `frame_ms`: one time for every step, or a list with one per step (16-10000 ms).
- `order`: which cell each step shows, at most 1024 steps. Without it every cell plays once, in order.
- `columns`: lays the cells out as a grid this many columns wide, read row by row. Without it the sheet is one row, so its height is the cell size.

A sheet holds at most 256 cells and is at most 16384 px on either side.

## Game files

Any `.png`, `.ttf`, `.otf` file under `assets/sprites/ui/` or `assets/fonts/` replaces the game's own file at the same path: the interface's art and its fonts. Images may be at most 4096x4096. Dump Resources writes every one of them, so the paths are right. Nothing else under `assets/` can be replaced: the game's own world art, sounds and music stay as they are, and clothing is never moddable.


## Themes

`theme.json` restyles the interface: theme (`hud`, `menu`, `system`, `game_corner`, `palette`) → control type → section (`colors`, `constants`, `font_sizes`, `fonts`, `icons`, `styles`) → item. Colours are `"#rrggbb"` or `"#rrggbbaa"`, font sizes 1-256, fonts and icons are paths under `theme/`. A style is an object of its properties; with `"class"` (`StyleBoxFlat`, `StyleBoxTexture`, `StyleBoxLine`, `StyleBoxEmpty`) it replaces the style, without one it changes the game's. `palette` holds the colours the game picks by state, under its one type `Palette` and section `colors`. Dump Resources writes the game's own `theme.json`, every item filled in.

One mistake anywhere in `theme.json` skips the whole file, so a half-applied theme never draws.

Control types can change between game versions, when one turns out to cover two parts of the screen. `pfmod check` cannot know which types a game version has, so a type the game does not have is not one of those mistakes: the game skips that type alone and names it in its log (Verbose Mod Debugs). After an update, dump again and compare.

Addon windows have types of their own in `hud`, so a theme can restyle them apart from the game's windows:

| Type | What |
|---|---|
| `AddonWindow` | An addon window's frame |
| `AddonWindowTitle` | Its title |
| `AddonLabel` | A line of text |
| `AddonButton` | A button |
| `AddonButtonSelected` | A button marked selected with `set_selected` |
| `AddonBar` | A progress bar |

## Limits

| What | Limit |
|---|---|
| Files in a mod | 20000 |
| One file | 64 MiB |
| Whole mod | 512 MiB |
| All scripts together | 2048 KiB |

A file that breaks a rule is skipped and reported; the rest of the mod still loads. Mods load in the order the Mod Management window lists them, and where two replace the same thing the lower one wins.
